const ans = `IDEA: geopull-exactquota
TITLE: Geodesic successor pull with capacity-exact (quota-preserving) deferred-acceptance SID assignment
MOTIVATION: The round-1 arm spent curvature on the radius of the latent ball and the codebook collapsed from 170 to 56 distinct triples (recall 0.0419, below its own parent). The round-2 arm multiplied the transport cost by a per-pair behaviour weight; margins moved but not one arg-min did, so the behaviour dependency was uncertifiable, and its frozen plan did not reproduce its column marginals. The real problem is therefore not "add more curvature" but: get behaviour into the arg-min as an ADDITIVE, order-changing term, and protect the per-level usage multiset EXACTLY rather than approximately. Recommendation-wise, what is missing in TIGER SIDs is that two items a user actually jumps between often land in different coarse prefixes, which destroys prefix-level next-item predictability.
NOVELTY: (i) The codebook is never moved and never re-parameterised: the curved operation acts only on the discrete assignment, so curvature cannot act as a radius/scale on the codebook. (ii) The curvature is spent as a DIRECTION and DISTANCE ALONG A GEODESIC set by the measured, null-standardised behaviour-graph curvature, not as a metric scale: kappa is fixed at 1 and delta_l only sets the geodesic fraction t_l. (iii) The assignment is a capacity-constrained deferred-acceptance (many-to-one Gale-Shapley) allocation whose output has the Euclidean per-level usage multiset EXACTLY by counting, not by a plan's arg-max - this is the direct answer to failure (b). (iv) Unlike the round-1 successor-Frechet codebook update, the successor Frechet mean here is a per-item additive bias on a quota-exact integer assignment, and unlike the round-2 cost reweighting it changes the arg-min by construction because it is added, not multiplied.
CHANGE: For every training item and every level, a hyperbolic Frechet mean of its training successors is pulled a curvature-determined fraction along the geodesic from the item, and the resulting point contributes an ADDITIVE bias to the item-code cost; the hard SID is then chosen by a capacity-exact deferred-acceptance pass whose per-code capacities are the Euclidean nearest-code counts, so the usage multiset is reproduced exactly while the membership, and therefore the gradient, is behaviour- and curvature-dependent.
SPECIFICATION:
Offline preprocessing (once, single process, CPU, TRAINING SPLIT ONLY):
  T[i,j] = number of training sessions in which item j occurs in the position immediately after item i (window 1); p_i(j) = T[i,j]/sum_j T[i,j].
  For each level l, take the frozen baseline prefix partition of the training items, build the quotient graph over codes, compute Ollivier curvature kappa_c (W1 between neighbour measures, unit edge lengths) and standardise against 20 member-shuffle nulls that preserve level sizes: z_l = (kappa_obs - mean_null)/sd_null, then centre over levels: delta_l = z_l - mean_l(z_l). The round-3 measured profile [-0.328,-0.071,+0.399] is the expected input.
  t_l = sigmoid(delta_l) in (0,1); written as 3 floats into the Stage-2 config. No tensor is exported, reduced or broadcast inside the training loop at any point.
Assignment refresh r (event-triggered: checked every 10 epochs, fired when the measured hard-assignment flip rate on a fixed 2048-item probe exceeds 0.05, capped at 30 refreshes per level per run; documented defaults):
  1. Euclidean pass over all 24556 training items: z_i, residuals r_i^l, and quotas m_c^l = #{i : c = argmin_c' ||r_i^l - e_c'^l||^2} (the BASELINE rule, so the protected multiset is the Euclidean one; sum_c m_c^l = N exactly, and codes unused by the baseline stay unused).
  2. x_i = tanh(||z_i||) * z_i/||z_i||, E_c = tanh(||e_c||) * e_c/||e_c|| (fixed unit Poincare ball, kappa = 1, no learnable radius, no learnable curvature).
  3. m_i = Frechet mean of the successor points under d_P: 5 Riemannian gradient steps from x_i, step size 1/sum_j p_i(j), projected back to radius 1-1e-3.
  4. g_i = exp_{x_i}( t_l * log_{x_i}( m_i ) ) (geodesic fraction t_l toward the behaviour centroid).
  5. cost(i,c) = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * [ d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) ].
  6. Solve the capacity-constrained allocation by deferred acceptance with capacities m_c^l, obtaining binary B. Assert sum_c B[i,c]=1 for all i and sum_i B[i,c]=m_c^l for all c; abort the refresh (keep the previous B) if either fails.
Training between refreshes: identical to the frozen RQ-VAE except the hard index is B(i,l) instead of the per-step arg-min; STE gradient as in the baseline. Ablation switches: ABL_BEHAVIOUR=0 sets p_i = delta_i (so m_i = x_i, g_i = x_i, bias identically zero); ABL_GEOMETRY=0 replaces d_P by Euclidean norm and m_i by the Euclidean weighted mean (g_i linear interpolation), keeping t_l; both switches default ON.
COST: Per training step the extra work is the hyperbolic map plus one extra distance row on 1024 items x 256 codes x 3 levels = 786k pairs, about +10-20% of the quantiser block (well under +5% of the total transformer step). Each refresh costs 3 x 24556 x 256 = 18.9M cost entries, 24556 x deg Frechet steps, and a deferred-acceptance solve of typically 3-6 rounds of 24556-item proposal sorts: about 0.2 s on one card, under a minute for 30 refreshes, under 1% of the 3000-epoch, 24-step-per-epoch run. No extra parameters, no extra seeds, no arm.
HYPOTHESIS: If successor-coherent items are placed into the same coarse prefixes under an exactly preserved usage histogram, then the level-1 hit rate stays at its baseline support (0.079/0.005) and the triple collision near 0.177, while prefix next-item predictability rises and Stage3 test_recall@10 moves above the 0.055537 baseline toward 0.065. Observable: the behaviour-off assignment differs from the both-on assignment on 20-60% of items at the last refresh (non-zero top-1 change is REQUIRED and is logged at every refresh), the usage-multiset assertion holds with equality at every refresh, and prefix transition entropy falls at fixed usage.
RISKS: The bias may over-pull items toward popular successor codes and destroy within-prefix diversity; deferred acceptance may produce worse-cost matchings than the Euclidean arg-min (it is stable, not optimal), so the reconstruction could degrade; event-triggered refreshes may lag the encoder; the standardised curvature delta may be too weak to set a useful t_l; the Euclidean quota may be a bad capacity target if the baseline usage is very skewed.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transitions from training sequences (next-item co-occurrence within a session, unit window), aggregated over the training split only.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Sparse count matrix T[i,j] over training sessions; row-normalised to p_i; used only through the weighted Frechet mean m_i and hence the bias d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c). Items with no successor get p_i = delta_i and zero bias. Recomputed once offline from the training split, never from validation or test.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T is built from the training interaction sequences only; the curvature profile is computed on the training-item prefix partition only; delta and t are frozen scalars in the config before Stage 2 starts; no validation/test interaction, no Stage-3 label enters the bias, the quotas or the assignment; the quota pass reads only training items.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare-ball distance d_P with fixed negative curvature kappa = 1 (unit ball), plus the exponential map exp_x and logarithm map log_x used for the geodesic interpolation exp_{x_i}(t_l log_{x_i}(m_i)); the standardised training-graph curvature delta_l sets t_l = sigmoid(delta_l), not the curvature itself.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the quantisation/assignment step of Stage-2 training, on every assignment refresh; it never touches the codebook parameters, the encoder parameterisation, or the latent radius.
COUPLING PATH: p_i -> m_i (Frechet mean under d_P) -> g_i (geodesic pull by t_l = sigmoid(delta_l)) -> additive bias -> cost matrix -> deferred acceptance -> hard SID B -> STE gradient and next-item prefix statistics. Removing behaviour sets the bias to zero; removing geometry replaces d_P and the Frechet mean by their Euclidean counterparts and changes g_i, so both change the arg-min and the gradient.
COUPLING EQUATION: cost(i,c) = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * [ d_P( exp_{x_i}( sigmoid(delta_l) * log_{x_i}( m_i ) ), E_c ) - d_P(x_i,E_c) ], with m_i = argmin_x sum_j p_i(j) d_P(x,E_j)^2.
OBSERVABLES: (1) top-1 flip count of B between the behaviour-on and behaviour-off cost at the final refresh (must be > 0 and is logged per refresh); (2) exact equality of the per-level usage multiset of B with the Euclidean m_c^l (asserted); (3) per-level distinct-code counts 247/7414/20223-scale support and collision near 0.177; (4) level-1 hit rates near 0.079/0.005; (5) prefix transition entropy and next-prefix predictability; (6) Stage3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: p_i = delta_i, hence m_i = x_i, g_i = x_i, the bracket is identically zero, cost reduces to the pure curved nearest-code cost, and B is the quota-exact curved assignment with no successor information.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa -> 0: d_P -> Euclidean norm, exp/log -> linear interpolation, m_i -> weighted Euclidean mean; the same additive bias, quotas and deferred acceptance are kept, so only the curvature is removed.
ABLATION BOTH ON: kappa = 1, geodesic fraction t_l = sigmoid(delta_l), successor Frechet means and the additive bias active, quotas exact; this is the single trained run.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  p_i(j) = T[i,j] / sum_k T[i,k]
  m_i^{(0)} = x_i; m_i^{(s+1)} = exp_{m}( eta * sum_j p_i(j) * log_{m}(x_j) ), eta = 1/sum_j p_i(j), s = 0..4, reproject to ||m|| <= 1-1e-3
  g_i = exp_{x_i}( t_l * log_{x_i}( m_i ) )
  C[i,c] = d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 + lambda_l * ( d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) )
  lambda_l = median_{i,c} d_P(x_i,E_c)^2 / median_{i,c} | d_P(g_i,E_c) - d_P(x_i,E_c) |, computed once at the first refresh and then frozen
  B <- DEFERRED_ACCEPT(C, m):  U = all items; while U not empty: each i in U proposes to its cheapest code not yet refused; each code c keeps its m_c cheapest proposals and refuses the rest; remove matched items from U
  assert sum_c B[i,c] = 1 and sum_i B[i,c] = m_c
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: training sequences (for T), training item latents z_i and Euclidean codebooks e_c^l at refresh time, quotas m_c^l, the frozen 3-vector delta. Outputs: a binary assignment tensor B of shape (N,3) giving one code index per level per item, plus the logged diagnostics (flip count, multiset assertion, collision, prefix entropy).
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||x|| and ||E|| to 1-1e-3 before artanh; artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-6; log_x(m) at m = x returns 0 (add 1e-8 norm guard); items with empty successor sets get zero bias; lambda_l guarded against a zero median denominator; the deferred-acceptance solve has a hard round cap of 4*K and falls back to the previous B (never to an unconstrained arg-min) if it does not terminate; exact-marginal assertion is a hard gate per refresh; no code may receive more than m_c items because capacity is decremented at accept time.
END IDEA`;
const r = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: ans});
return r;
